types.d.ts-1117-    /**
types.d.ts-1118-     * Persist `batches` in order, each as one ordinary atomic commit with its own seq, checked against the state the
types.d.ts-1119-     * earlier ones left, in as few round trips as the backend can. Every batch has at least one write: a commit without
types.d.ts-1120-     * writes never reaches Storage, so the Session never sends an empty batch. Stops at the first batch Durable's own checks refuse
types.d.ts-1121-     * (global IDs, document actions, copy resolution): the batches before it are durable, it and the ones after are not.
types.d.ts-1122-     * Calls `receive(index, seq)` once per durable batch, in order, synchronously, after all of them are durable and
types.d.ts-1123-     * before the next commit starts. Resolves with the number of durable batches and the refusal, if any. Rejects for an
types.d.ts-1124-     * unknown outcome (connection lost, statement or commit failed); `receive` calls made before the rejection still
types.d.ts-1125-     * stand. `receive` is a durability receipt, not publication: the Session publishes later. Once it resolved, later
types.d.ts-1126-     * reads through this storage observe the stored batches.
types.d.ts-1127-     */
types.d.ts-1128-    commit(batches: readonly (readonly StorageWrite[])[], receive: (index: number, seq: Seq) => void, context: Context): Promise<CommitResult>;
types.d.ts-1129-    /**
types.d.ts-1130-     * Optional. Run `publish`, the Session's publication of one stored or held commit (its cache write-through,
types.d.ts-1131-     * adoption, and observers), inside this storage's own scope, such as a store's attached host batch, so what the
types.d.ts-1132-     * publication marks lands together. Call `publish` exactly once, now or soon after; the Session publishes the next
types.d.ts-1133-     * commit only once it ran. Without it, the Session publishes directly.
types.d.ts-1134-     */
types.d.ts-1135-    publishing?(publish: () => void, context: Context): void;
types.d.ts-1136-    /**
types.d.ts-1137-     * Return a fresh branded candidate from the Session-global numeric ID namespace, greater than every ID minted since
types.d.ts-1138-     * this storage was opened and every ID stored, also across reopen: scans order by ID as creation order, and the
types.d.ts-1139-     * Harness relies on it.
types.d.ts-1140-     */
